reconstruction: D01: For every universe-polymorphic type α with Countable and Infinite instances and every class H, if every member of H is infinite, existence of one G2 element strategy succeeding eventually on every presentation of every member is equivalent to a G1 Nat-indexed inner cover by infinite sets.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: D01: ∀{α : Type u}[Countable α][Infinite α], ∀H, (∀L∈H, Infinite L) → (EM(H) ↔ HasCountableInnerCover H). Expand EM as ∃e ∀L∈H ∀s, Presents s L → ∃T ∀t≥T; expand the cover as ∃C, (∀i, Infinite(C i)) ∧ (∀L∈H, ∃i, C i⊆L). e/C precede L,s; T and the cover index may depend on L, and T on s.
algorithm_scope: D01: G0–G2. The learner receives the sample list and delayed correctness bits according to G2. No membership-query channel or named strategy is part of this type.
limitations: D01: No nonempty-class hypothesis or bound on T; empty H still needs strategy/cover witnesses. Duplicate cover sets and repeated samples are permitted. This is an iff of existence properties, not equality of procedures or computability. reconstruction: D02: Under the same Countable, Infinite, and all-targets-infinite assumptions, existence of a G3 infinite-set strategy whose representative receives feedback and whose whole output is eventually fresh and contained in the target is equivalent to existence of a G2 element strategy.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: D02: ∀{α : Type u}[inst : Countable α][Infinite α], ∀H, (∀L∈H, Infinite L) → (SM_inst(H) ↔ EM(H)). Each side has its own ∃strategy ∀L∈H ∀presentation ∃T ∀t≥T. SM uses the displayed Countable instance in its chosen rank map and representative feedback.
algorithm_scope: D02: G0, G2, G3. The set strategy always outputs an infinite set. Its feedback tests the least-ranked representative for target membership and sample freshness, while success tests containment of the entire set. Both schedules have delayed feedback.
limitations: D02: No assertion that a given element/set pair have equal outputs, equal thresholds, or identical feedback histories. Set output nonemptiness and infinitude are certificates of the strategy, including off-run histories; mere truth of a representative reply is not full-set correctness. quantifiers_and_dependencies: D03: ∃H : Set (Set Nat), EQ(H) ∧ ¬SQ(H). The first conjunct is ∃(q,o), ∀L∈H ∀s presenting L, ∃T ∀t≥T, output∈L\A_{t+1}. The negated conjunct denies existence of any (q,S,infinitude certificate) satisfying ∀L∈H ∀s presenting L ∃T ∀t≥T, output⊆L\A_{t+1}.
algorithm_scope: D03: G0, G4. Each query sees samples through index t and earlier bits; output sees the current query answer as well. The theorem names no separating class or particular strategy; those existential witnesses are not recoverable from the withheld theorem proof.
limitations: D03: No UUS/all-targets-infinite, class-nonempty, cardinality, rate, or explicit class description is a conjunct. reconstruction: D04: For a Countable infinite universe and a class whose every language is infinite, existence of one G4 set-query strategy succeeding eventually on every target presentation is equivalent to a countable inner cover by infinite sets.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: D04: ∀{α : Type u}[Countable α][Infinite α], ∀H, (∀L∈H, Infinite L) → (SQ(H) ↔ HasCountableInnerCover H). SQ expands to ∃(q,S,certificate) ∀L∈H ∀presentation ∃T ∀t≥T. The cover is chosen before the target-dependent containment index.
algorithm_scope: D04: G0, G1, G4. Each round has one membership query, then an infinite set output using the current answer; success is whole-set containment in L minus all t+1 observed samples. No named implementing strategy is in this endpoint.
limitations: D04: Both directions preserve semantic rather than effective existence. Set infinitude holds at actual rounds before T as well; correctness need only hold after T. Empty H and repeated cover sets are allowed. reconstruction: D05: For every Nat-indexed family of classes on a Countable infinite universe, if every language in every indexed class is infinite, two implications hold together: if every indexed class admits EM, their union admits EM; and if every indexed class admits SQ, their union admits SQ.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: D05: ∀{α : Type u}[Countable α][Infinite α], ∀classes : Nat→Set(Set α), (∀i L, L∈classes i → Infinite L) → ((∀i, EM(classes i)) → EM(⋃i,classes i)) ∧ ((∀i, SQ(classes i)) → SQ(⋃i,classes i)). Premise strategies may depend on i; each conclusion chooses one strategy for the whole union before L and its presentation. ∃T remains run-dependent.
algorithm_scope: D05: G0, G2, G4. The two branches retain their respective sample/reply schedules. The type does not provide an effective selector from i to a strategy, and the union learner is not given a hidden target index.
limitations: D05: Both implications are retained; neither is an iff here. Classes may repeat, overlap, or be empty, and a target may belong to several indices. There is no finite-union restriction, common time bound, or uniform program certificate on the family. Shared limitation: Stage 1 semantic reconstruction only; no source comparison, proof-body review, fresh build, computability certification, or human certification. reconstruction: D06: For a Countable infinite universe and all-infinite target class, the conjunction of two implications holds: EM implies a no-sample correctness-feedback element strategy ZEM; SQ implies a no-sample set-query strategy ZSQ.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: D06: ∀{α : Type u}[Countable α][Infinite α], ∀H, (∀L∈H, Infinite L) → (EM(H)→ZEM(H)) ∧ (SQ(H)→ZSQ(H)). Each no-sample conclusion independently has ∃strategy ∀L∈H ∃T ∀t≥T, with no presentation quantifier. ZEM requires x_t∈L; ZSQ requires S_t⊆L with global actual-round infinitude.
algorithm_scope: D06: G0, G2, G4, G5. ZEM sees prior membership/correctness bits and emits before its current reply. ZSQ issues a membership query using t and prior bits, and its infinite set output sees the current answer. Neither receives sample elements.
limitations: D06: No freshness or pairwise novelty conclusion is present for either zero-example predicate. No converse or identity of premise and conclusion strategies is claimed. reconstruction: D07: Under Countable, Infinite, and all-targets-infinite assumptions, two characterizations hold together: ECM is equivalent to a countable inner cover, and ECQ is equivalent to a countable inner cover. ECM and ECQ must tolerate arbitrary finite initial reply errors on arbitrary sample streams as specified in G6.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: D07: ∀{α : Type u}[Countable α][Infinite α], ∀H, (∀L∈H, Infinite L) → (ECM(H)↔HasCountableInnerCover H) ∧ (ECQ(H)↔HasCountableInnerCover H). algorithm_scope: D07: G0–G2, G4, G6. No Presents premise may be added. ECM output sees t+1 samples and only t observed bits; ECQ output sees t+1 samples and t+1 bits, including the current observed answer. ECM success is element membership and freshness; ECQ success is entire infinite-set containment outside all observed samples.
limitations: D07: N and T need not coincide, be known, or have a uniform rate. The feedback premise constrains only a tail of v. Repeated/off-target sample values are allowed. reconstruction: D08: For any infinite type α with DecidableEq and any target class H, assume that every no-feedback element generator that succeeds on H has its freshened generator self-lock along every presentation of every target in H. Under that explicit assumption, existence of a no-feedback infinite-set generator is equivalent to existence of a no-feedback element generator. D09: For every type α and target class H, existence of a no-feedback generator producing infinite fresh target subsets eventually along all target presentations implies existence of a no-feedback element generator correct and sample-fresh eventually along all those presentations.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: D08: ∀{α : Type u}[inst : Infinite α][DecidableEq α], ∀H, (∀g, IsLimitGenerator g H → SelfLocksAlongEveryPresentation (freshenedGenerator_inst g) H) → (SG(H)↔G(H)). The premise expands to ∀g, successful(g) → ∀L∈H ∀s presenting L, ∃n, [ListWithin P_n(s) L ∧ ∀tail, ListWithin tail L → correct((freshened g),L,P_n(s)++tail)]. Existential SG/G witnesses and their per-run T follow that assumption. D09: ∀{α : Type u}{H : Set(Set α)}, SG(H) → G(H). SG means ∃S, global all-history infinitude ∧ ∀L∈H ∀s presenting L ∃T ∀t≥T, subset and disjointness. G means ∃g ∀L∈H ∀s presenting L ∃T ∀t≥T, membership and freshness.
algorithm_scope: D08: G0, G7, G8. No feedback or membership queries occur. Freshening preserves an already sample-fresh output and otherwise classically chooses a universe-fresh point. The locking assumption refers to freshened g, not g itself, and quantifies all successful g. D09: G0, G7. There are no typeclass premises at this endpoint, including no Nonempty, Infinite, Countable, or DecidableEq premise. Both learners see only the finite sample tuple. No named selection procedure is asserted by the type.
limitations: D08: This endpoint is conditional; the self-locking premise must not be dropped. No Countable instance is required. Locking is correctness after every finite target-valued extension, not constancy of output; n may depend on g,L,s. No effective method for finding n or implementing choice is provided. D09: The antecedent retains its all-history infinite-set certificate, even when target obligations are vacuous. This is only the displayed implication and does not independently establish the reverse direction or a computational transformation. reconstruction: D10: For the G9 named universe, target, generator, and base stream, four statements hold together: (1) the generator is a limit element generator for the singleton class containing target; (2) it is fresh on every finite sample tuple, including off-target tuples; (3) basePresentation presents target; and (4) no prefix of basePresentation is a self-locking history for that generator and target.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: D10: IsLimitGenerator gap.generator {gap.target} ∧ (EverywhereFresh gap.generator ∧ (Presents gap.basePresentation gap.target ∧ ¬∃n, IsSelfLockingHistory gap.generator gap.target (P_n(gap.basePresentation)))). Conjunct (1) expands to ∀L∈{target} ∀s presenting L ∃T ∀t≥T, membership and sample freshness. Conjunct (2) is ∀t xs, freshness. Conjunct (4) denies ∃n [within(prefix,L) ∧ ∀tail within L, correct(prefix++tail)].
algorithm_scope: D10: G0, G7–G9. This endpoint fixes all four named objects; the spike test compares the full ordered history to the G9 spike list. On a spike the output is inr 0; otherwise it is a classically selected unseen target element. No oracle or persistent state beyond the input tuple is used.
limitations: D10: All four conjuncts are retained. The no-lock assertion concerns prefixes of this particular base presentation, not every presentation or every finite history. The type does not say the generator fails to generate its target; the first conjunct explicitly asserts success. Proofs of the branch properties and convergence were not examined. reconstruction: D11: For every nonempty Countable type α and every target class H, existence of a finite inner cover of H by infinite sets suffices for no-feedback element generation in the limit on H. D12: There exists a target class H over Nat such that every language in H is infinite, H is no-feedback element-generatable in the limit, and H has a countable inner cover by infinite sets. D13: There exists a target class H over Nat × Nat whose every language is infinite and which is no-feedback element-generatable in the limit, but which has no finite inner cover by infinite sets.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: D11: ∀{α : Type u}[Nonempty α][Countable α]{H : Set(Set α)}, HasFiniteInnerCover H → G(H). The premise packages ∃m C, (∀i : Fin m, Infinite(C i)) ∧ (∀L∈H, ∃i, C i⊆L). The conclusion is ∃g ∀L∈H ∀s presenting L ∃T ∀t≥T, g-output∈L and outside A_t(s). D12: ∃H : Set(Set Nat), UUS(H) ∧ (G(H) ∧ HasCountableInnerCover H). Thus after H: ∀L∈H, Infinite L; independently ∃g ∀L∈H ∀s presenting L ∃T ∀t≥T, correct and fresh; independently ∃C : Nat→Set Nat, (∀i Infinite(C i)) ∧ (∀L∈H ∃i C i⊆L). D13: ∃H : Set(Set(Nat×Nat)), UUS(H) ∧ (G(H) ∧ ¬HasFiniteInnerCover H). After H, the successful generator is ∃g ∀L∈H ∀s presenting L ∃T ∀t≥T, membership and sample freshness. The last conjunct denies existence of any m, C : Fin m→Set(Nat×Nat), global component-infinitude certificates and target-dependent containment indices.
algorithm_scope: D11: G0, G1, G7. No feedback channel, given presentation index, or named algorithm occurs. Nonempty and Countable are actual assumptions; Infinite α is not an outer assumption. Existential g may depend on the class and available cover existence, and T may depend on L,s. D12: G0, G1, G7. The declaration existentially asserts the class, generator, and cover through the indicated predicates; it names none of them. Only the generator sample-history interface is known, with no feedback or effective enumeration guarantee. D13: G0, G1, G7. The universe is exactly the product Nat×Nat, not the G9 sum. No named class, no named generator, and no query access are given; the existential witness is not extracted from a proof body.
limitations: D11: A size-zero finite cover is allowed for an empty target class; no nonempty-class condition is added. Every covered target contains an infinite member of the cover. There is no converse, effective compiler, named witness, or rate guarantee here. D12: There is no class-nonempty condition, no assertion that finite inner covers fail, no properness or minimality of the countable cover, and no rate. The witness cannot be identified by inspecting a withheld theorem proof or importing a familiar example. D13: The negation ranges over every finite size, including zero, and every possible such cover, with no effective restriction. A countable-cover property is not an explicit conjunct of this endpoint. All three positive/negative components are retained; no computational or rate claim is added. Shared limitation: Stage 1 semantic reconstruction only; no source comparison, proof-body review, fresh build, computability certification, or human certification.
